marks.gloss_en: the redactor's appended block (ואמר רבה בר מחסיא אמר רב חמא בר גוריא אמר רב ... אמר רב חסדא: ובו ביום) shows why a dream fast cannot be borrowed: it works only on that very day. The link is the stam's juxtaposition, not the guest's argument; Rav's כאש לנעורת and Rav Yosef's ואפילו בשבת ride along as committed dicta only
Rav: a fast is good for a dream as fire is for chaff
אמרו ליה רבנן לרב ששת: הא קא חזינן רבנן דמסיימי מסנייהו ואתו לבי תעניתא!
איקפד ואמר להו: דלמא מיכל נמי אכול -- perhaps they ate too; their practice proves nothing
the rabbanan to Rav Sheshet: we see rabbanan who wear their shoes and come to the fast-house
(they had prepared a third-grown calf: ליטעום מר מידי) ולוזיף מר וליפרע, לא סבר מר להא דאמר רב יהודה אמר רב: לוה אדם תעניתו ופורע? (kind svara: no ObjectionKind for an amoraic memra)
תענית חלום הוא (= p_taanit_chalom_hu)
Rav Yehoshua b. Rav Idi: I am sitting in a fast
(asked: what is dozing?) Rav Ashi: asleep and not asleep, awake and not awake -- called, he answers; he cannot give a reasoned reply; reminded, he remembers
Rav: an individual who accepted a fast is forbidden to wear shoes
Abaye [and Rava] wore [their shoes] on the upper
Rav: a person borrows his fast and repays [it]
Shmuel (איכא דאמרי): obvious! let it be no more than a vow -- may one not repay a vow tomorrow or another day?
קדשו צום קראו עצרה -- כעצרת: as work is forbidden on an assembly-day, so on a fast
בשלמא כולהו אית בהו תענוג -- bathing, smearing, relations; אבל מלאכה צער הוא! work is suffering, not pleasure
Rav Chisda in R' Yirmeya bar Abba's name: 'sanctify a fast, call an assembly' -- the fast is like the assembly-day, on which work is forbidden (= p_yirmeya_melacha_kaatzeret)
R' Yirmeya bar Abba: the verse says 'sanctify a fast, call an assembly' -- like an assembly-day: as work is forbidden on it, so on a fast
אספו זקנים -- דומיא דאסיפת זקנים: as the gathering of elders is by day, so the fast is by day (R' Zeira reporting R' Yirmeya bar Abba)
מסייע ליה לרב הונא -- the 'gathering of elders' comparison supports Rav Huna's morning gathering
אי מה עצרת מאורתא אף תענית נמי מאורתא! -- if a fast is like the assembly-day, work should be forbidden from the evening before
R' Zeira, as R' Yirmeya bar Abba explained to him: 'gather the elders' -- like the gathering of elders, by day (= p_yirmeya_tzom_bayom)
ואימא מטיהרא? -- then say [the fast is] from noon
Rav Sheisha b. Rav Idi: מסייע ליה לרב הונא, דאמר מצפרא כינופיא -- the gathering is from the morning
R' Yirmeya bar Abba (as R' Zeira had it from him): 'gather the elders' -- like the gathering of elders, which is by day, the fast too is by day
the mishna: on the second three fasts they are forbidden in work, bathing, smearing, wearing shoes and marital relations
the mishna: these [last seven] exceed the first ones in that on them they sound the alarm and lock the shops

Abaye: from morning to midday we look into the town's affairs; then a quarter of the day we read in the Torah and the haftara; then we ask for mercy -- as it says 'they read in the book of the Torah a quarter of the day, and a quarter they confessed and prostrated' (Neh 9:3)
if these passed and they were not answered, they reduce business dealings
